newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bond prices up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bond prices up in thin trade.

text.p: Israeli bonds, except those linked to the dollar, closed higher on Tuesday in thin trade, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.08 pct to 169.26.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct at 160.03
Volume was low at 125 million shekels with bonds linked to the consumer price index (CPI) rising for the fifth consecutive day, traders said.
"Long inflation-linked bonds continue to rise sharply, but activity is falling because institutional investors are less active now," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.

"All the rises were concentrated in the long bonds and the short CPI-linked bonds closed almost unchanged. Yields are now around 4.5 percent and at the current rate the market will remain stable," said Roy Meir at Simodan.

"Unlinked bonds continue to rise but at a much slower pace. Despite that, the bonds are still very attractive with yields of 16.4 percent and (1996) inflation expectations of around 10 percent," the Mizrahi trader said.

"Makams (which are also unlinked) rose mildly following the Bank of Israel's tender (on Tuesday). The yields on the Makams issued today were relatively low at 15.1 percent as against market yields of 15.2 percent," Meir said.
Traders said that total volume in the Makams was low at 31 million shekels as investors prefer longer bonds, such as the Gilon.
Traders noted that dollar-linked bonds continued to fall as the dollar weakens against the shekel.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2380 shekels against 3.2430 on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
